nodes.name: H₄xdp Ligand Synthesis
nodes.procedure: The ligand was synthesized by reacting alpha, alpha’-Dibromop-xylene with triethyl phosphite and followed by refluxing the obtained oil with conc. hydrochloric acid according to the literature method [41]. Block colorless crystals were obtained from the water solution by slow evaporation.
nodes.source_text: 2.1 Synthesis of p‑Xylylenediphosphonic Acid (H₄xdp) ... Block colorless crystals were obtained from the water solution by slow evaporation.

nodes.name: Mo-MOF Precursor Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Na₂MoO₄·2H₂O (0.240 g, 1.0 mmol) was stirred together with p-xylylenediphosphonic acid (H₄xdp) (0.140 g, 0.5 mmol) in 16 mL deionized water. The pH of the solution was adjusted to 1 by dropwise addition of conc. hydrochloric acid. The acidified solution was then placed in a 25 cm³ Ace pressure tube and heated at 120 °C for 15 h. The resultant white crystalline material was thoroughly washed with deionized water several times and dried at 80 °C for 12 h under vacuum.
nodes.source_text: 2.2 Synthesis of [(MoO₂)₂(xdp)(H₂O)₂]·2H₂O ... dried at 80 °C for 12 h under vacuum.

nodes.name: Pyrolysis to MoP@PC
nodes.procedure: 500 mg Mo-MOF precursor was placed in a porcelain boat. Then, the boat was heated at 900 °C under a constant flow of N₂ at 30 mL min⁻¹ for 120 min with the warming rate of 20 °C min⁻¹. The final black powder was collected when the temperature dropped to room temperature under N₂.

unit_operations.name: Pyrolysis
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: the boat was heated at 900 °C under a constant flow of N₂ at 30 mL min⁻¹ for 120 min with the warming rate of 20 °C min⁻¹

nodes.source_text: 2.3 Preparation of MoP@PC Nanowires ... The final black powder was collected when the temperature dropped to room temperature under N₂.

nodes.name: Electrochemical Activation
nodes.procedure: The in situ electrochemical activation was carried out in 0.5 M H₂SO₄ under a N₂ atmosphere to avoid possible oxidation caused by O₂ in air. This was conducted by using the three-electrode system of CHI 760E electrochemical workstation. MoP@PC was used as the working electrode, carbon rod as counter electrode, Ag/AgCl (saturated KCl filled) as reference electrode. Performed by cyclic voltammetry (CV) from -0.2 to 0.2 V vs RHE for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: 2.4 Electrochemical Activation ... cycle voltammetry (CV) from -0.2 to 0.2 V vs RHE in 0.5 M H₂SO₄.

nodes.characterization_summary: FESEM shows regular nanowire morphology with diameters ranging from approximately 200 to 300 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FESEM of MoP@PC (Fig. 2b) shows that the MoP@PC has a regular nanowire morphology, similar to that of the Mo-MOF precursor (Fig. 2a).

properties.features: high aspect ratio nanostructures, bundled fibers, turquoise false color (likely staining)

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows nanowire structures consisting of MoP cores surrounded by thick graphite shells (~10 layers).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In Fig. 2d, e, the HRTEM shows that the nanowire structures consist of MoP cores and graphene shells (Fig. 2d).

properties.description: Thin layer observed in TEM image

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows crystal planes with d-spacing of 0.28 nm corresponding to the (100) lattice of MoP nanoparticles and graphite shells with interlayer distance of 0.34 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HRTEM image in Fig. 2e clearly shows the crystal planes with a d-spacing of 0.28 nm, corresponding to the (100) lattice of the MoP nanoparticles.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows D band (≈1323 cm⁻¹), D' band (1600 cm⁻¹), G band (≈1568 cm⁻¹), D₄ band (≈1200 cm⁻¹), and D₃ band (≈1490 cm⁻¹) indicating disordered graphite structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The deconvoluted D (≈1323 cm⁻¹) and D' (1600 cm⁻¹) bands originate from defects... The low ratio of the G band demonstrates the existence of a highly disordered graphite structure.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM-EDS mapping shows uniform distribution of phosphorus, carbon, and molybdenum without significant aggregations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The uniform distribution without significant aggregations of phosphorus, carbon, and molybdenum is observed through TEM energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Mo 3d peaks at 228.3, 231.5 eV (Mo³⁺), 229.0, 233.5 eV (Mo⁴⁺), 234.4, 236.2 eV (Mo⁶⁺); P 2p at 129.5, 130.4 eV (P in MoP), 133.8 eV (PO₄³⁻/P₂O₅); C 1s at 284.6 eV (graphitic), 286.1 eV (C-P), 288.5 eV (C=O); O 1s at 530.2 eV (C-O), 532.2 eV (Mo oxides).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3a–d shows the typical high-resolution XPS profiles of Mo 3d, P 2p, C 1s, and O 1s in the MoP@PC, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Nitrogen adsorption/desorption isotherm shows specific surface area of 11.7 m²/g for MoP@PC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nitrogen adsorption/desorption isotherm at 77 K of MoP@PC indicating the specific surface area of 11.7 m² g⁻¹ (Fig. S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: C K-edge XANES comparison shows increased π* and σ* peak intensities for A-MoP@PC indicating improved graphitization, peak at 288 eV (interlayer state) confirming ultrathin graphene layers, and 288.4 eV (Mo-P-C bonds) showing chemical interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For A-MoP@PC, the intensity of the peaks for π* and σ*, increased significantly, indicating that the graphitization degree of A-MoP@PC is improved... The peak located at about 288 eV of A-MoP@PC can be attributed to a graphene analog of the interlayer state in graphite... The peak at 288.4 eV can be ascribed to Mo–P–C bonds.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of A-MoP@PC shows stronger Mo 3d peaks at 227.9 and 231.8 eV (Mo³⁺) and P 2p peak at 129.8 eV indicating improved MoP penetration after carbon layer removal.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In comparison with the Mo 3d (Fig. 3a) and P 2p (Fig. 3b) profiles of MoP@PC, the stronger peaks of Mo 3d (Fig. 5c) at lower binding energies (227.9 and 231.8 eV) can be assigned to Mo³⁺, and the peak located at 129.8 eV of P 2p (Fig. 5d) proves the improved penetration of MoP for A-MoP@PC.

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of A-MoP@PC shows thinner surface carbon layers (1-3 layers) compared to original MoP@PC.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM and HRTEM images in Fig. 5g, h, for A-MoP@PC, show that the nanowire structure is maintained well after electrochemical activation, and the surface carbon layers become thinner than the MoP@PC.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman of A-MoP@PC shows disappearance of D₄ band (amorphous carbon dissolution) and G band at ≈1577 cm⁻¹ confirming preservation of stable graphitic carbon.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 5i shows the Raman spectra of sample A-MoP@PC, which significantly differs from that of MoP@PC... The disappearance of the D₄ band demonstrates the dissolution of the amorphous carbon during electrochemical activation.

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ adsorption/desorption shows specific surface area of 14 m²/g for A-MoP@PC with no significant change in pore size distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. S9, the A-MoP@PC displays similar N₂ adsorption/desorption isotherm with MoP@PC, the specific surface area of A-MoP@PC is 14 m² g⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV shows double-layer capacitance Cdl of 5.2 mF cm⁻² for A-MoP@PC (vs 0.9 mF cm⁻² for MoP@PC), corresponding to ECSA of 148.7 cm².
nodes.evidence_snippet: The calculated Cdl values... of MoP@PC and A-MoP@PC (Fig. 4d) are 0.9 and 5.2 mF cm⁻², respectively. The corresponding ECSA values are 22.9 cm² for MoP@PC and 148.7 cm² for A-MoP@PC.
